summary: This article explains how plastic trash reaches the ocean, why it harms sea animals and breaks into tiny pieces, how currents gather it, and how people clean it up and keep it out of the sea.
introduce: Ask students to share a small problem they solved this week and how they solved it, and write two examples in a Problem | Solution chart on the board. Tell them that “Cleaning the Oceans” also has a problem and a solution to find.

keyTerms.def: trash left lying on the ground in a public place
water or air that keeps moving in one direction

challengeTerms.def: a tiny piece of plastic, smaller than a grain of rice
scattered pieces of waste or broken things
to catch or twist up in something so it is hard to get free

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that keeping trash out of the ocean is easier than cleaning it up? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a plastic bottle dropped in a city could end up in the ocean, and one way to stop it.
struggling: Pre-teach litter, source, and current with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use microplastic, debris, and entangle in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
